synthesis.executive_summary: Real demand, real margin problem. Students want this and would pay, but the unit economics only work at a delivery density the plan does not explain how to reach. The operational and legal timelines are also longer than budgeted.
consensus_points: The pain point is genuine and students articulate it unprompted.
Batch density, not menu quality, decides whether this survives.
The launch timeline underestimates food-safety registration.

disagreements.topic: Whether the margin problem is fatal or solvable

sides.The Economist: Negative contribution margin at current pricing is structural, not a scale problem.
sides.The Operator: Margin turns positive at eight deliveries per route; that is reachable in one hostel cluster.

disagreements.resolution: Both are right at different densities. Prove eight-per-route in a single cluster before raising on the model.

disagreements.topic: Whether the demand model is a differentiator
disagreements.sides: The User and The Operator see it as invisible plumbing; The Critic argues it is complexity added before product-market fit is proven.
disagreements.resolution: Ship a fixed menu first. Add routing once you have four weeks of real order data to route on.

strengths: Subscription revenue that can be forecast against kitchen capacity.
A user who describes the problem in their own words without prompting.
weaknesses: Contribution margin is negative below eight deliveries per route.
Semester breaks create churn the plan does not account for.
opportunities: Hostel-level bulk contracts remove the last-mile problem entirely.
Menu data becomes a supply-planning asset within two semesters.
threats: Incumbent aggregators can undercut on delivery for as long as it takes.
A single food-safety incident ends the business.
action_plan_7_days: Interview twenty students across three hostels about their current meal spend.
Rebuild the unit economics with delivery cost as a variable, not a constant.
Start the FSSAI registration; it gates everything downstream.
action_plan_30_days: Run one hostel block with a fixed menu and measure deliveries per route.
Sign a letter of intent with one hostel administration.
Decide on the demand model only after four weeks of real order data.
synthesis.final_recommendation: Do not raise money on this yet. The demand is real enough to justify six weeks of work, but the margin story is unproven and the panel splits precisely on whether density is reachable. Run a single hostel block, measure deliveries per route, and let that number decide whether this is a business or an expensive way to feed people.
